comments.author: matsix
comments.body_html:
An update - Just want to put some info out there on the status of this mod, I am kinda obsessed with clouds atm… This mod has become a serious problem for me and I feel like I won’t stop until the clouds are some of the best out there. (I have ridiculous expectations of myself)

I have been working on this more since the day I released on here. A new update will be coming (hopefully) this weekend. Two of the big things I have listed for future updates will be coming - Much improved erosion and micro detail. I went through the hassle of making a whole noise generator in Unity that lets me preview the noise before generating it. So I was able to make a proper 3d noise map for the clouds so they are shaped better than ever. I also reviewed the paper from Guerrilla Games a lot closer and found some neat shader tricks that they showed direct code for (there’s more than one paper on how they do their clouds). So pretty much everything will be improved about how the clouds look across the board. How sharp they are, how light transfers through them, how the cloud shadows are handled etc…

comments.author: matsix
comments.body_html:
One thing that I couldn’t figure out a good value for and just set to something that I thought looked cool is ambient strength. The color might be a bit strong for some people, if you turn it down a bit it should mute the color a bit.

Play with some other settings too. A lot of settings can have a big change on the look of the clouds. For example, if you want more wispiness where you have more finer detail, increase detail erosion between 15-20%. If you break the look of anything, just reset all the settings back.

Keep in mind, the finer detail you add, the more noise you will see. You can increase primary steps to counter it. (enable advanced bepinex settings to increase primary steps further)

comments.author: matsix
comments.body_html: Yeah not a good idea to use this with low-end graphics card. By default, I have the clouds rendering at half res, but to help even more, you can lower the primary steps from 64 down to like 30-40, just keep in mind, the lower the steps, the more noise you will get. Some people might not be bothered by it if they aren’t hyper focused on the clouds. You can lower the light steps a bit too, those are actually significantly more expensive but the shader is designed to work with 6 light steps set.
